departments.description: The Emergency Unit provides 24-hour urgent medical care for patients with serious injuries, acute illnesses, and life-threatening conditions. The unit is equipped with resuscitation bays, a triage area, and emergency treatment rooms.
departments.location: Block A, Ground Floor — left wing, directly opposite the main entrance
departments.nhis_notes: Emergency care provided first, registration follows. NHIS covers emergency visits.

departments.description: The Clinical Laboratory provides diagnostic testing services including blood tests, urine analysis, microbiology, clinical chemistry, and haematology. Results are typically available within 2-4 hours for routine tests.
departments.location: Block B, First Floor — above the Pharmacy
services: Blood tests (FBC, RBS, FBS, HbA1c, Lipid profile)
departments.nhis_notes: All routine laboratory tests are covered by NHIS. Some specialised tests may require payment.

departments.description: The Maternity Ward provides comprehensive maternal and child health services including antenatal care, delivery services, postnatal care, and family planning. The ward has a labour suite, delivery rooms, and a postnatal ward.
departments.location: Block C, First Floor — access via the east staircase
services: Immunisation (BCG, OPV, Hepatitis B at birth)
PMTCT (Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of HIV)
departments.nhis_notes: NHIS covers antenatal visits, delivery, and postnatal care under the free maternal care policy.

departments.description: The NHIS Desk assists patients with health insurance registration, renewal, and claims processing. All patients are encouraged to register with the NHIS to access subsidised healthcare services.
departments.location: Block A, Ground Floor — near the main entrance, adjacent to OPD registration
services: Information and counselling on insurance benefits
departments.nhis_notes: Bring your Ghana Card for NHIS registration. Annual premium starts from GH¢30 for adults.

departments.description: The Outpatient Department handles patients who require medical consultation but do not need to be admitted. Services include general consultations, vital signs check, and referrals to specialist clinics.
departments.location: Block A, Ground Floor — near the main entrance
departments.nhis_notes: NHIS card accepted. Please bring your valid NHIS card and Ghana Card.

departments.description: The Hospital Pharmacy dispenses prescribed medications to both inpatients and outpatients. The pharmacy stocks a wide range of medicines including essential drugs, chronic disease medications, and emergency supplies.
departments.location: Block B, Ground Floor — next to the OPD
departments.nhis_notes: NHIS covers most essential medicines. Some branded drugs may require co-payment.

faqs.question: What time does the hospital open?
faqs.answer: The hospital opens at 7:30 AM from Monday to Friday. OPD operates until 5:00 PM. The Emergency Unit is open 24 hours every day.

faqs.question: Does the hospital accept NHIS?
faqs.answer: Yes, the hospital accepts NHIS. Please bring your valid NHIS card and Ghana Card for registration at the NHIS desk.

faqs.question: How do I get a medical certificate?
faqs.answer: Visit the OPD for a consultation. After examination, the doctor can issue a medical certificate. A fee of GH¢20 applies.

faqs.question: Where do I go for malaria testing?
faqs.answer: Visit the OPD first for assessment. The doctor will request a malaria test if needed. Tests are done at the Laboratory on Block B, First Floor.

faqs.question: What should I bring for my antenatal visit?
faqs.answer: Please bring your NHIS card, Ghana Card, previous ANC records (if any), and your maternity passport.

faqs.question: How much does NHIS registration cost?
faqs.answer: Annual NHIS premium starts from GH¢30 for adults. Children under 18, elderly above 70, and pregnant women are exempt from premium payments under the NHIS policy.

faqs.question: What are the emergency contact numbers?
faqs.answer: Emergency: 024-412-3457. Ambulance: 193. National Emergency: 112. Police: 999.

faqs.question: Do you offer family planning services?
faqs.answer: Yes, family planning services are available at the Maternity Ward. Services include counselling, contraceptive pills, injections, implants, and IUD insertion.

faqs.question: How long do laboratory results take?
faqs.answer: Routine tests like malaria RDT, blood sugar, and urine analysis take about 30 minutes to 1 hour. More complex tests like culture sensitivity may take 24-48 hours.

faqs.question: Where is the Pharmacy located?
faqs.answer: The Pharmacy is located on Block B, Ground Floor, next to the OPD. Operating hours are 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM on weekdays and 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM on Saturdays.

faqs.question: Can I refill my chronic medication?
faqs.answer: Yes, the OPD handles prescription refills for chronic conditions like hypertension and diabetes. Please bring your previous prescription and any medical records.

faqs.question: What immunisation services are available at birth?
faqs.answer: Newborns receive BCG (tuberculosis), OPV (polio), and Hepatitis B vaccines at birth at the Maternity Ward. These are free under the national immunisation programme.

faqs.question: What is the address of the hospital?
faqs.answer: The hospital is located on Hospital Road, opposite the Central Market, P.O. Box 123, Kumasi.

faqs.question: Do you have an eye clinic?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Ophthalmology Department runs eye clinics every Tuesday and Thursday from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM. Please register at the OPD first.

faqs.question: How do I get a referral to a specialist?
faqs.answer: Visit the OPD for assessment first. The general practitioner will refer you to the appropriate specialist if needed. Bring any previous medical records.

faqs.question: What laboratory tests are covered by NHIS?
faqs.answer: Routine tests such as blood count, malaria test, urine analysis, blood sugar, and stool examination are covered. Specialised tests may require additional payment.

faqs.question: Do you have dental services?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Dental Department offers consultations, extractions, fillings, and oral health education. The clinic is open Monday to Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

faqs.question: What is the visiting hours for patients?
faqs.answer: Visiting hours are from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM on weekdays and 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM on weekends. Please limit visitors to two per patient.

faqs.question: How do I access my medical records?
faqs.answer: Visit the Records Office (Block A, Ground Floor) with a valid ID. There is a GH¢10 fee for medical record retrieval.

faqs.question: What should I do in a pregnancy emergency?
faqs.answer: Go directly to the Maternity Ward (Block C, First Floor) or call 024-412-3460. For severe emergencies, call 112 or 193 for an ambulance.
